notes: Central Bedfordshire does not run a selective or additional licensing scheme. Its only property licensing policy covers houses in multiple occupation under the national mandatory rules. Check with the council if you are unsure about your property.
research: Three separate council indexes checked, none containing a selective or additional scheme. (1) The housing policy register lists exactly four private-sector policies: a 'Houses in Multiple Occupation Licensing Policy', a Housing Enforcement Policy (under review), a Rogue Landlords Database Policy, and a Civil Penalty Policy under the Renters' Rights Act 2025. LOWEST CONFIDENCE IN BATCH: this is a negative by exhaustive absence, not an explicit denial. Central Bedfordshire publishes no public-facing HMO licensing page at all; its HMO Licensing Policy sits behind a SharePoint link that could not be read. Re-check if a definitive page appears.

notes: Chelmsford states plainly that it has no additional or selective licensing schemes. Only the national mandatory HMO licence applies, for homes where five or more people in two or more households share facilities. The fee starts at £900.
research: The council states this explicitly on its own HMO licensing page: 'We do not have Additional or Selective licensing schemes in place.' The sitemap was parsed and the only HMO-related pages are the licensing page, temporary exemption notices and the two public registers.
